Puto Bumbong

Served at: Gaudete Sunday

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Puto Bumbong is a traditional Filipino purple rice cake steamed in bamboo tubes, commonly enjoyed during the Christmas season, especially on Gaudete Sunday. It is a festive delicacy often served after the Simbang Gabi mass, symbolizing the joyful anticipation of Christmas.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups glutinous rice flour
  • 1/2 cup purple yam (ube) powder or natural purple food coloring
  • 1/4 cup sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup water
  • Banana leaves for lining (optional)
  • 1 cup grated mature coconut
  • 1/2 cup muscovado sugar or brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup melted butter or margarine

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine glutinous rice flour, purple yam powder, sugar, and salt.
  2. Gradually add water and mix until a thick, sticky batter forms.
  3. If using banana leaves, soften them by briefly heating over an open flame or boiling water, then cut into strips to line the bamboo tubes.
  4. Fill each bamboo tube halfway with the batter, then steam the tubes vertically over boiling water for about 15-20 minutes until the puto bumbong is cooked through and firm.
  5. Carefully remove the rice cakes from the bamboo tubes and place on a serving platter.
  6. Brush the puto bumbong with melted butter or margarine while still warm.
  7. Top with grated coconut and sprinkle muscovado sugar generously before serving.

Tips

  • If purple yam powder is unavailable, use natural purple food coloring or mix in cooked, mashed ube for color and flavor.
  • Banana leaves add traditional aroma and prevent sticking but can be omitted if unavailable; use parchment paper instead.
  • Serve warm immediately for the best texture and flavor.
